clue.text: Slander 28 with malice, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged some other way

parts.note: the answer to 28 across, a female relative

explanation.surface: Someone slanders a relative out of spite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' shuffles AUNT (the answer to 28) with MALICE.
explanation.definitionFit: To calumniate is to make false and damaging statements about someone, a formal synonym for slander.

clue.text: Male face left out

indicators.note: out means the letter for left is dropped from the slang word

parts.note: clock is British slang for a person's face

explanation.surface: A man's face has its left side missing.
explanation.walkthrough: CLOCK is British slang for a face ('nice clock'); 'out' removes L.
explanation.definitionFit: A cock is the male of a bird, especially a domestic fowl.

clue.text: Brand of goods — mature stock

parts.note: a product line is a brand or range of goods
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A shop's own-brand range becomes established stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock in the sense of ancestry or descent, as in 'of noble stock'.

clue.text: Original Amazon journey?

parts.note: a ship's first trip, read whimsically as the trip of a female warrior, since an Amazon is a young woman of legend

explanation.definitionFit: A ship's first trip at sea is its maiden voyage, maiden meaning first and also a young woman, like an Amazon.

clue.text: One Latin student bound to restrict metre at the wrong moment

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
L is a learner driver, a student

indicators.note: to restrict means the tied word holds the metre letter within it

parts.note: bound means tied

explanation.surface: A Latin student is obliged to keep to the metre but comes in at the wrong moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to restrict' puts M inside TIED, giving TIMED after I, L, L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mistimed happens at an inconvenient or inappropriate moment.

clue.text: No officers turning up among the best soldiers

indicators.note: among means the reversed ranks sit inside the word for the best

parts.note: the tops are the best

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Among the finest soldiers, no officers appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses OR (other ranks, the non-officers) to RO, which goes 'among' TOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops are soldiers collectively, an army's men.

clue.text: Schoolgirl is in the middle of writing

indicators.note: in the middle of means the word is goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: MS is a manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl sits halfway through her essay.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss is a name for a girl or young unmarried woman, as a schoolgirl is.

clue.text: Some suntan aid I rigged up, resembling a bright arc

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read from bottom to top
some means only part of these words is used

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a stand of suntan lotion that gleams like a rainbow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks NAIDIRI from 'suntan aid I rigged'; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Iridian means relating to or like a rainbow, after Iris, goddess of the rainbow.

clue.text: Not good enough to be paid by the minute?

definitions.text: to be paid by the minute?
definitions.meaning: jokingly, a rate of pay worked out per short unit of time

explanation.definitionFit: Second-rate means inferior, and a rate per second would be a pay rate for tiny timespans.

clue.text: Money evil? (No-one will return a huge amount)

parts.note: a cent is a small coin, money
ill means evil, as in ill will

indicators.note: will return means these two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Is money the root of evil? Nobody gets back a vast sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will return' reverses NO + I (one) to give ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A centillion is an enormous number, ten to the power 303, hence a vast quantity.

clue.text: The last character in chapter has a galvanising result!

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: The final twist in a chapter gives a thrilling ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Galvanising is coating steel with zinc, so the metal is what that process produces a layer of.

clue.text: Struggling companies mostly lack politeness

indicators.note: struggling suggests a disorderly mix of the letters
mostly means the last letter of the word lack is dropped

explanation.surface: Firms in difficulty tend to lack good manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts LACK to LAC; 'Struggling' shuffles COMPANIES with LAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaisance is obliging courtesy, a willingness to please others.

clue.text: Late party — and what it may do to the neighbours?

definitions.meaning: a gathering after a death, with the late person mourned

definitions.text: what it may do to the neighbours?
definitions.meaning: a noisy party may rouse people next door from sleep

explanation.definitionFit: A wake is a vigil or gathering for the dead, and to wake is to rouse from sleep.

clue.text: Behold Jerusalem after the Emperor's collapse

indicators.note: after places the next two pieces later in the answer than the emperor

parts.note: IMP is short for imperator, Latin for emperor
lo is an old word for behold
Sion, or Zion, is a name for Jerusalem

explanation.surface: After the emperor's fall, see Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: An implosion is an inward collapse.

clue.text: Wow! Reading is ruined by book's errors

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: is ruined suggests the word Reading is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Wow! A reading is spoiled by mistakes in the book.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation like 'gosh'; 'is ruined' scrambles READING to RIGENDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrigenda are a list of errors in a printed work, with their corrections.

clue.text: 'General plan will be finished by six' we retorted

parts.note: over means finished
VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: retorted, read as turned back, means the word we is reversed

explanation.surface: Someone retorts that the overall scheme will be done by six o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: An overview is a general survey or outline of a matter, a broad plan of it.

clue.text: Beginner's work Magritte, say, kept back

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work

indicators.note: kept back means the painter's first name is read backwards

parts.note: René Magritte, the Belgian surrealist painter

explanation.surface: A novice's piece by Magritte is held in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: An opener is something that begins, such as the first item or a starter.

clue.text: Local dignitary called US city up about start of riots

indicators.note: about means the word for called goes around the letter
in a down clue up means the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: named means called
LA, Los Angeles

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of riots

explanation.surface: A local official phoned an American city about the start of riots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses NAMED and LA together to ALDEMAN; 'about' wraps that round R, the 'start of' riots.
explanation.definitionFit: An alderman is a senior member of a local council, a civic dignitary.

clue.text: Fish caught in a flash may have this look

definitions.text: Fish caught in a flash may have this look

parts.words: Fish caught in a flash may have this look
parts.note: a fish named for its colouring, and the glowing pupils in a photograph taken with a flash

explanation.definitionFit: Red-eye is the scarlet pupils from camera flash, and also a name for the rudd, a freshwater fish.

clue.text: City in Germany, with resident disowning it?

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany

indicators.note: disowning means the letters of it are removed from resident

explanation.surface: A German city whose resident rejects it.
explanation.walkthrough: D is Germany's international car code; 'disowning' strips out the I and T, not as a block but one letter at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden is the capital of Saxony, a city on the Elbe.

clue.text: Get over skin wound for sure

parts.note: to clear an obstacle is to get over it
a cut is a wound in the skin

explanation.surface: Get over a graze, certainly.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear-cut means definite and unambiguous, certain.

clue.text: Direct broadcasting service?

definitions.meaning: to steer or guide something along a course

explanation.definitionFit: To channel is to direct, and a channel is a TV or radio station.

clue.text: Also-ran is out, say, having gone round third of course

indicators.note: having gone round means the outward word encloses the letter

parts.note: forth means out, as in go forth

indicators.note: third of means the third letter of course

explanation.surface: A losing horse is out, having gone round the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having gone round' puts U, 'third of' course, inside FORTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Finishing fourth means missing the first three places, so the horse is an also-ran.

clue.text: This bird could supply yer eggs (with two duck-eggs thrown in)

indicators.note: thrown in means the two round letters go inside the rearranged letters
could supply suggests the letters of yer eggs could be made into something else

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, shaped like O, so two give OO

explanation.surface: A bird that could provide your eggs, with a couple of duck eggs added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could supply' rearranges YER EGGS to GREYGSE; 'thrown in' puts OO inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The greylag or grey goose is a wild goose, a large bird.

clue.text: Just a little tailless fish

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a shade means just a little, as in a shade too long

explanation.surface: A small fish with no tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The shad is a herring-like fish.

clue.text: Drop the rent

definitions.meaning: a drop of liquid from the eye
a split or rip in cloth

explanation.definitionFit: A tear is a drop shed when crying, and also a rip in fabric.

clue.text: Draw attention to missing debut of girl stripper

indicators.note: missing means the letter is taken out

parts.note: to nudge someone is to prod them to draw their attention

indicators.note: debut of means the first letter of girl

explanation.surface: A girl stripper is noticed for missing her first night.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripper ends up naked, and a nude is an unclothed figure.

clue.text: In favour of pit closing initially in North-East? That'll get you notoriety

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a mine is a pit

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the compass abbreviation
initially means the first letter of closing

explanation.surface: Backing pit closures in the North-East will make you notorious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes C from 'closing'; 'in' puts it inside NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Prominence is the state of being widely known or conspicuous, akin to notoriety.

clue.text: Sally perhaps losing her head?

indicators.note: losing her head means the first letter goes

parts.note: a sally is a witty jibe, a taunt

explanation.surface: A woman named Sally loses her head.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aunt Sally is a fairground figure whose head is knocked off by thrown sticks; a sally is also a taunt, here losing its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunt Sally is a British fairground target, so a relative named Sally fits the whole clue.

clue.text: Treasury minister to risk returning a wad of money?

parts.note: to chance something is to risk it

indicators.note: returning means the word for a wad of notes is read backwards

parts.note: a roll is a wad of banknotes

explanation.surface: Should a finance minister gamble on getting back a bundle of cash?
explanation.walkthrough: The Chancellor of the Exchequer is the UK finance minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chancellor heads the UK Treasury, the chief finance minister.
